items.title: Jev Can SERIOUSLY Supercharge Your AI Second Brain (Here's How)
items.summary: My AI second brain makes thousands of decisions every day. Which emails are safe, which ones need a reply, which news is worth my time, which ideas I've already seen. items.title: The Biggest AI Coding Agent Upgrade Is Already on Your Machine?!
items.summary: Every conversation you have with your coding agent is saved as a file on your machine - every prompt, every tool call, every failure. It's a goldmine of data that almost nobody takes advantage of, and it's the best way I've found to make my coding agent better over time. So in this video I show you two ways to use it! The simple way is one prompt that has your coding agent go through your past conversations and suggest the top improvements for your rules, hooks, and skills. The full way puts everything into structured tables in a database (I use Databricks), so you can easily query it with your coding agent and MCP. It's super token efficient too! I also show you the real changes I made to my own AI layer from it (I'm actually keeping every one of them). ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ - Check out Databricks Free Edition - free to use, no credit card, and everything in this video runs on it: https://databricks.plug.dev/xLkLORm Thanks to Databricks for working with me on this video! Btw - the "not used to train" commitment I show ~10 minutes in is from Databricks' paid terms. items.title: Why Your Company Needs a Context Graph (and How to Build It) — Gil Feig, Merge
items.summary: Your agent can tell you why one customer was upset. Ask which customers were upset last year, and it falls apart. Gil Feig, co-founder and CTO of Merge, explains why every company needs a context graph, a company brain that brings together third-party data, structured context, memories and skills. Using the question "which customers were upset last week?", he shows why connecting a few MCP servers isn't enough: live API lookups can't search across large datasets, so you need a synced copy for semantic queries, alongside live calls for simple lookups. He walks through the architecture: a router, synced and live context, a summarizer, and skills and memory that encode how your company actually defines things like a happy customer. He covers four tiers of context including derived summaries, a decision flowchart for when to use cache or live data, and why every answer must keep track of where its data came from. In this talk: • Why MCP live lookups can't answer questions across large datasets • Combining synced data, live lookups, a router and a summarizer • Why company skills and memory belong in the context layer • Traceability: where data came from, when, and what invalidates it SPEAKER Gil Feig, Co-founder & CTO, Merge LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/gilfeig/ X: https://x.com/gilfeig LINKS Merge: https://www.merge.dev Merge Agent Handler: https://www.merge.dev/merge-agent-handler Merge Gateway: https://www.merge.dev/gateway Merge on X: https://x.com/merge_api CHAPTERS…

items.title: Meta Muse AI Connectors: The App Store for AI?
items.summary: In this solo episode, I break down the huge business opportunity because Meta has opened Muse, its personal AI agent, to developers. You can now submit a connector, which lets Muse use your service when someone asks it for help, and I think this could be the app store moment for AI. I explain how a connector works, share four startup ideas you can build on one, and cover how to get customers beyond Meta's directory. I also show how I'd build a first version with a coding agent like Claude Code or Codex, and what I'd test before submitting it to Meta for review.
